contacts.institution: unspecified authorities ('they') who picked him up after a maintenance worker called it in
contacts.when: about age 9 (c. 1970-71), after he ran away at a bus rest stop
contacts.what_was_asked: None stated; a maintenance worker reported a child on the rest-stop roof
contacts.what_institution_did: Picked him up, kept him overnight in a church in Modesto and sent him to his aunt's in San Francisco; his mother then took him back into the temple.
contacts.quote: And after being there for a few days, I guess, while one of the maintenance workers had realized that there was somebody up on the roof and it called it in. I ended up going to... They picked me up. I spent the night in some church in a Modesto, I think. And then they sent me to my aunt's in San Francisco.
contacts.what_happened_next: He told his aunt/uncle what was going on and his uncle offered to keep him, but his mother took him back and he was sent to a temple family who beat him with a rubber hose.
contacts.notes: Who 'they' were is not stated, nor whether the abuse was raised with them (he says he told his uncle and aunt). Recorded because an outside body took custody of him in connection with his running away; may not meet the 'harm reached' test.

contacts.what_institution_did: Kept the boys there; the leader's son and then the leader's wife were brought, and on the cult leader's say-so the shackles were cut off with air-driven cutting wheels.
contacts.quote: So anyway, he goes and gets his mother. She comes over there and she looks and she tells them the same thing. Keep them here. And she leaves and then she comes back and she says [perpetrator] said to take our father said to take the shackles off.
contacts.what_happened_next: The shackles came off, but he returned to the discipline/learning crew under an overseer who beat children with a stick; abuse continued until November 1978.
contacts.notes: Institution was the abuser's own (institution_was_abusers); the removal was ordered by the cult leader himself, so it is not counted as protection. The cutting caused another burn.

contacts.what_was_asked: To leave Jonestown with the congressman's party
contacts.what_institution_did: Accepted the defectors' request and put them on the truck to the airport to leave with his party; the party was then attacked by temple gunmen at the Port Kaituma airstrip.
contacts.quote: So the next thing Ryan knew is he had a group on his hands that wanted to leave. Everything wasn't rosy and paradise. contacts.notes: Tom saw a note passed to reporters and told his father; the family went together to Ryan. Initiated_by could also be 'person' (Tom took part).

contacts.when: after rescue, from about November 21, 1978, for a month
contacts.what_was_asked: Treatment for the gunshot wound to his leg
contacts.what_institution_did: Treated his leg for about a month.
contacts.quote: And the next morning, they flew us out. And then I was in the George Town Hospital for a month, recovering from my leg.
contacts.what_happened_next: Returned to the US with family.
contacts.notes: Gunshot wound reached a medical provider; standard treatment.

contacts.when: on return to the United States, late November 1978

contacts.notes: Coded per the rule that taking information with no further step shown is did_nothing_or_delayed; the cult leader was already dead, so the season does not show what action was called for. 'unclear' would also be defensible. Jim gives a parallel account at s4-e6 @ 8:17.

persons.outcome_quote: Tom and his sisters were finally rescued from the jungles of Guyana after two nights, three days on November 20, 1978.
persons.decisive_work_quote: I think it's important to highlight that without the push of Congressman Ryan and journalists like Tim Reiterman investigating Jonestown, the Boge family, as well as the other defector families may not have lived that day.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: November 18, 1978 (Ryan's visit), roughly eight years after his first runaway at age 9 and about 13 years after the family joined
persons.notes: Captivity ended through the congressman's delegation, which the family approached after Tom saw a note passed to reporters; but he was shot while leaving and the cult leader died the same day, so coded partly_protected rather than protected. The show credits both Ryan and journalists (decisive_work_by unclear); Ryan's visit was itself prompted by Bob Houston's father, the Concerned Relatives and an Examiner article. Two age-9/age-14 runaways ended with him returned to the temple by his mother. 'Other' never-reached reason: physical captivity/isolation in Jonestown - his escape bid toward the Matthew's Ridge military post and the US consulate was caught. His 2013 essay was read on air. After return: nightmares, drugs, homelessness (s4-e6 @ 13:27). Media later retraumatised him (journalists, not an institution under the rubric). Also mentions being slugged by a stranger at 19 and scammed at 22 (s4-e6 @ 20:06) - passing anecdotes with no aftermath, not given separate records. months figure is approximate (age 9 ~1970).

coder_notes: Season 4 (Something Was Wrong, 'Escaping Jonestown'): the Bogue family's time in the Peoples Temple (1965-1978), defection with Congressman Ryan's party, the Port Kaituma airstrip attack and the aftermath. Large parts of each episode are narration from Steven Hassan's and Stephanie Sarkis's books, excerpts from Raven and A Thousand Lives, and ads/music filler.
